title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 113
paragraphs: Meanwhile Xerxes with his army remained for a few days after the sea-fight, and then they all began to march off toward Boeotia by the same route they had come. Mardonius thought it was good both to escort the king on his way and also that it was now too late in the year to carry on the war; it was better, he reasoned, to winter in Thessaly and then at the beginning of spring to attempt the Peloponnese. When he reached Thessaly, Mardonius first chose for himself all those Persians called the “Immortals,” except their commander Hydarnes (for Hydarnes said he would not be left behind by the king); then, from the other Persians, those who wore cuirasses and the body of a thousand horse; and also the Medes, Sacans, Bactrians, and Indians, both foot and horse. These nations he took en masse, but from the other allies he picked out only a few at a time, choosing those of fine appearance and those whom he knew had rendered good service. From the Persians he took more than from any other single nation, and these wore collars of twisted metal and bracelets; after them came the Medes, who were not inferior in number to the Persians, only in bodily strength. The result was a force of three hundred thousand in all, including cavalry.
